speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you have a history of a psychiatric condition and have noticed a new movement disorder; can you describe exactly what movements you are experiencing and when they first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Since you started risperidone two months ago, have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or involuntary movements since beginning the medication? Also, how severe are these movements on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms sound very much like akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. Have you noticed any worsening of these feelings after taking your dose or if you have missed a dose? Also, do you experience any muscle stiffness or jaw clenching (tremors) alongside the restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history; it helps rule out substance-induced causes. To differentiate between akathisia and other extrapyramidal symptoms, have you noticed any muscle stiffness, jaw clenching (bruxism), or tremors? Also, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or drooling?
